note: Rio Grande NF (Conejos Peak RD) beside the Alamosa River, ~9,700 ft, two miles below Stunner Pass; the old Stunner mining townsite is just east. Access is dirt FR 255 / FR 250 / FR 380. --Claude
summary: FS campground page: confirmed 5 sites, vault toilet, no water, free, phone 719-274-8971; no recreation.gov listing so FCFS. Added the forest's 14-day limit. Season left unset (page contradicts itself). Note cleaned of field facts, the fishing remark and the internal waterfront remark. Flags: Oct 2026 flood damage on FR 250 both ways (4WD recommended / impassable), riverview doubtful.
flags: Phone 719-274-8971 confirmed (Conejos Peak Ranger District, on the FS page).

ROAD / 4WD (criteria): Rio Grande NF conditions page after the Oct 22 2026 storm: 'FSR 250 between Stunner to Highway 17 has damage - 4WD is recommended - Conejos Peak Ranger District' and 'Forest System Road (FSR) 250 between the Alamosa Guard Station and the Science Camp is impassable - road damage - Conejos Peak Ranger District'. The FS directions come in from La Jara on FR 255 then FR 250 up the Alamosa canyon; the other way out is FR 250 over Stunner Pass to CO-17. Forest alert (Oct 23, updated Oct 26): 'We encourage the public to avoid venturing out to the Forest when possible.' The campground page itself still reads 'Site Open'. EKKO is not 4WD.

Road (normal conditions): the FS page has no road-surface or RV wording beyond 'Motorized access may be limited by snow and annual seasonal road closures from March 15th to May 15th.' FR 250 in Alamosa Canyon has a 20 mph speed-limit order. Conejos Peak road status table (May 29 2026): 250 Stunner Pass listed. No length figure anywhere.
Season conflict on the FS page: current conditions 'Open year-round.' vs 'Seasons of Use: Late-May to Mid-October'. Left season unset.

Waterfront (stored riverview, looks generous): on imagery the loop sits on an open meadow bench; the Alamosa River here is ~8-12 m wide (creek-sized by the curation doc's 30 m rule) and runs ~100-200 m east and south-east of the loop behind a belt of spruce, so a sightline from the sites is doubtful. Suggest not waterfront; left for the waterfront gate.
